theme: 3 terms on app extensions: the small view of your app on the Home Screen, the separate program type it belongs to, and the shared container they both use

terms.definition: A small view of your app's content on the Home Screen or Lock Screen, built with WidgetKit.
terms.example: The Widget shows today's step count, tapping it opens the app.
terms.code:
import WidgetKit
// after saving a note in the app
WidgetCenter.shared
    .reloadTimelines(ofKind: "Notes")

terms.definition: A separate small program inside your app that adds a feature to the system, like a widget or a share sheet action.
terms.example: The share sheet item is an App Extension, so it has its own memory limit.

terms.definition: A shared container that lets your app and its extensions read and write the same data.
terms.example: Put the database in the App Group, so the widget can read it.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let shared = UserDefaults(
    suiteName: "group.com.example.notes")!
shared.set(3, forKey: "unread")
print(shared.integer(forKey: "unread"))

quizzes.question: In this code, what does the suite name point to?
What shows a small view of your app on the Home Screen?
What do you call a separate small program that adds a feature to the system?

video.title: Widget, App Extension & App Group | Day 95
video.description:
Learn to explain how widgets and other extensions share data with the app: Widget, App Extension & App Group, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Widget - A small view of your app's content on the Home Screen or Lock Screen, built with WidgetKit.
App Extension - A separate small program inside your app that adds a feature to the system, like a widget or a share sheet action.
App Group - A shared container that lets your app and its extensions read and write the same data.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: iOS Widget, App Extension & App Group | Day 95
landscape.description:
Explain Widget, App Extension & App Group in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
위젯, 앱 익스텐션, 앱 그룹 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Widget - A small view of your app's content on the Home Screen or Lock Screen, built with WidgetKit.
한국어: 위젯: WidgetKit으로 만들어 홈 화면이나 잠금 화면에 앱 내용을 작게 보여주는 뷰

App Extension - A separate small program inside your app that adds a feature to the system, like a widget or a share sheet action.
한국어: 앱 익스텐션: 위젯이나 공유 시트 동작처럼 시스템에 기능을 더하는, 앱 안의 별도 작은 프로그램

App Group - A shared container that lets your app and its extensions read and write the same data.
한국어: 앱 그룹: 앱과 그 익스텐션이 같은 데이터를 읽고 쓸 수 있게 해 주는 공유 컨테이너

landscape.hook: The widget always shows zero. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why does the widget say zero?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the Widget always shows zero unread, even with new messages.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the problem. The Widget is an App Extension, with its own container.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Widget reads a completely different store?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Every App Extension gets its own. Share data through an App Group.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I save with the App Group suite name instead?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, in both the app and the Widget. Same group name.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, or the Widget waits for its next scheduled timeline update.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. One App Group, and the App Extension sees the same `unread`.

dialogue.code:
// in the app, after a new message
UserDefaults.standard
    .set(unread, forKey: "unread")
WidgetCenter.shared
    .reloadTimelines(ofKind: "Inbox")
